title: The Message First to Smyrna Sent
description: The Message First to Smyrna Sent in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 137, “Smyrna. Rev 2:11”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The mes-sage first to Smyr-na sent, A mes-sage full of grace; To all the Sa-vior's flock is meant, In ev-ery age and place.

lines: The message first to Smyrna sent,
A message full of grace;
To all the Savior's flock is meant,
In every age and place.
Thus to his church, his chosen bride,
Saith the great First and Last;
"Who ever lives, though once he died,
Hold thy profession fast.
Thy works and sorrows well I know,.
Performed and borne for me;
Poor though thou art, despised and low,
Yet who is rich like thee?
I know thy foes, and what they say,
How long they have blasphemed;
The synagogue of Satan, they,
Though they would Jews be deemed.
Though Satan for a season rage,
And prisons be your lot;
l am your friend, and I engage
You shall not be forgot.
Be faithful unto death, nor fear
A few short days of strife;
Behold! the prize you soon shall wear,
A crown of endless life!"
Hear what the holy Spirit saith
Of all who overcome;
"They shall escape the second death,
The sinner's aweful doom!"

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
